items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear (durabilityManager, processEntry, retainedJobs), but the core logic has almost no comments. The worker's spin on `b.applied`, the WaitGroup rerouting in commitWrite (`walSyncWG = &entry.walWG`) and the retention-eviction `break` are all unexplained.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: durability.go is 668 lines. waitForJobDurability runs about 90 lines and waitForDurability about 80. The condition `(seqNum == 0 && m.totalDurableCommits > 0) || (seqNum > 0 && m.highestDurableSeqNum >= seqNum)` and the firstErr/closed checks are pasted 6+ times. It adds a separate worker goroutine instead of a hook in commit.go.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: The worker polls with `for !entry.b.applied.Load() { runtime.Gosched() }`, which the conventions forbid. `m.queue <- entry` can block the commit pipeline once 4096 entries are queued. Durations are clamped to `time.Nanosecond`, so they can be fake. Default-callback detection uses fragile `reflect...Pointer()` comparison. Errors are latched and propagated.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: The API is additive. But every sync commit now takes `m.mu`, allocates a job and a chan in newJobID, allocates an entry, and hops through a worker goroutine, even when BatchDurable is unset. The apply error path now runs `b.applied.Store(true)`, a behaviour change.
